page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EASv4 series, featuring a constrained-core configuration designed for memory-intensive workloads that require lower core counts for software licensing optimization. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock frequency of 3.525 GHz. Cache allocation comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 128.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 16.0 GB per allocated vCPU.

Local ephemeral storage consists of a 275 GB SSD, offering fast temporary workspace and swap storage. The instance does not include dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Compute performance across standardized synthetic tests is balanced to modest: Geekbench yields scores of 1,604 in single-core and 6,375 in multi-core execution, while PassMark logs a CPU score of 11,895.86. Memory benchmarks display a cached read bandwidth of 515.14 GB/sec, dropping to 39.27 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 22.62 GB/sec for uncached writes. Synthetic stress-ng evaluations register lower compute saturation, placing single-core and multi-core throughput in the lower brackets.

Workload execution is well suited for in-memory databases, caching engines, and mid-tier transactional databases. The instance achieves 8.29 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and demonstrates 10.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-only machine learning inference remains limited, producing 15.36 prompt tokens per second and 6.29 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Because memory capacity is coupled with reduced active vCPUs, the server delivers high cost efficiency for relational database management systems and enterprise applications where per-core software licensing costs dominate infrastructure expenses.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. Configured as a constrained-core instance, it exposes 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a dense 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Ephemeral local storage is provided via a 275 GB SSD, with no integrated GPU acceleration. Across benchmarks, the server demonstrates balanced performance, recording 1,604 in single-core Geekbench, 11,895.86 in PassMark CPU, and 8.29 million operations per second in Redis SET throughput. While raw compute scaling remains moderate under heavy multithreaded loads, the substantial memory footprint and reduced core count optimize operational costs for commercial database engines, in-memory caches, and enterprise software bound by per-core licensing.
